methodology.data_source: iShares (BlackRock) public product-screener API — the same feed that powers ishares.com's own retail fund finder
methodology.vehicle: ETF only (excludes traditional index funds and ETPs/ETCs)
methodology.domicile_note: iShares has no Spain-domiciled products — only Ireland, UK, Luxembourg, Germany and Switzerland exist in their catalogue
methodology.listing_preference: London Stock Exchange (LSE) preferred when available, for buyability on UK/European retail platforms
methodology.sharpe_calc: 3-year annualized return ÷ 3-year annualized volatility, from daily close prices, risk-free rate assumed 0%
methodology.sanity_filter: annualized return outside -80%..+150% is treated as corrupt price data and discarded, not shown

# Analysis of Top 10 iShares Equity ETFs by 3-Year Sharpe Ratio

## 1. Fund-by-Fund Commentary

**iShares MSCI Europe Financials Sector UCITS ETF (ESIF.L)** — Sharpe 1.918
Tracks European financial-sector equities (banks, insurance, diversified financials). The highest return in the set (36.86%) combined with moderate volatility (19.22%) produced the top-ranked Sharpe ratio, suggesting a strong multi-year run for European financials rather than unusually low volatility.

**iShares MSCI World Financials Sector Advanced UCITS ETF (WFNS.AS)** — Sharpe 1.875
A global version of the financials theme. Lower absolute return than its European counterpart (28.49%) but also meaningfully lower volatility (15.2%), showing that global diversification within the sector tempered swings while still capturing sector-wide gains.

**iShares Russell 1000 Value UCITS ETF (R1VL.L)** — Sharpe 1.594
Tracks large-cap US value stocks. The lowest volatility in the top three (12.63%) alongside a solid 20.13% return illustrates how a value-style, lower-beta US exposure can generate an efficient risk-adjusted outcome even without the highest raw return.

**iShares S&P 500 Scored and Screened UCITS ETF (ESPX.AS)** — Sharpe 1.572
An ESG-screened variant of the S&P 500. Return (21.95%) and volatility (13.97%) both sit close to broad US market behavior, indicating the screening did not materially alter the risk/return profile relative to standard large-cap US exposure.

**iShares MSCI USA ETF (CSUS.SW)** — Sharpe 1.553
Broad-based US equity exposure with the lowest TER in the list (0.03%). Return/volatility (22.27%/14.34%) is representative of the general US equity market over the period, reinforcing that broad US beta was a strong contributor to Sharpe ratios across this list.

**iShares S&P 500 Communication Sector UCITS ETF (IUCM.L)** — Sharpe 1.481
Sector-specific exposure to US communication services (mega-cap media/internet/telecom). Higher volatility (17.42%) than broad US funds was offset by a higher return (25.8%), consistent with concentrated sector behavior.

**iShares S&P 500 Paris-Aligned Climate UCITS ETF (UPAD.L)** — Sharpe 1.454
A climate-tilted S&P 500 variant. Return (20.82%) and volatility (14.32%) are close to standard S&P 500 characteristics, suggesting the Paris-alignment screening did not significantly change the fund's risk/return shape versus the broad index.

**iShares MSCI World Communication Services Sector Advanced UCITS ETF (WCMS.AS)** — Sharpe 1.432
Global counterpart to the US communication sector fund. Similar return (25.49%) but slightly higher volatility (17.8%) than the US-only version, indicating the global expansion added some volatility without proportional return benefit in this window.

**iShares MSCI Europe Mid Cap UCITS ETF (EUMD.L)** — Sharpe 1.43
European mid-cap equities. The lowest return in the top 10 (18.12%) paired with correspondingly low volatility (12.67%) produced a competitive Sharpe ratio primarily through volatility control rather than return generation.

**iShares S&P 500 Information Technology Sector UCITS ETF (IITU.L)** — Sharpe 1.418
US tech-sector exposure. The highest volatility in the entire list (22.22%) was paired with a high return (31.51%), but the elevated volatility pulled the Sharpe ratio to the bottom of this top-10 group despite strong absolute performance.

## 2. Thematic Concentration and Bias

Several concentration patterns are evident in this set:

- **US equity dominance**: 7 of 10 funds have exposure primarily or entirely to US equities (R1VL.L, ESPX.AS, CSUS.SW, IUCM.L, UPAD.L, WCMS.AS partial, IITU.L), indicating the ranking is heavily tilted toward US market performance over this 3-year window.
- **Sector concentration**: Financials appear twice (ESIF.L, WFNS.AS), and communication services appear twice (IUCM.L, WCMS.AS) — both in US and global/regional variants. Technology (IITU.L) is also represented. This suggests cyclical/growth sectors and financials performed particularly well in risk-adjusted terms over the period.
- **Currency exposure**: The majority of top funds are USD-denominated (US and global funds), with only two EUR-denominated European funds (ESIF.L, EUMD.L) in the top 10, implying USD-based returns played a significant role in the ranking outcomes for GBP/EUR-based investors, subject to unhedged currency movements.
- **Domicile uniformity**: All 10 funds are Ireland-domiciled UCITS ETFs; no UK- or Luxembourg-domiciled funds appear, and no LSE-preference conflicts arose since Irish domicile was already the common base.
- **Listing split**: 6 of 10 funds are LSE-listed; the remaining 4 (WFNS.AS, ESPX.AS, CSUS.SW, WCMS.AS) trade only on Euronext Amsterdam or SIX Swiss Exchange, meaning UK/European investors seeking LSE access would have a narrower subset (6 funds) to choose from within this top-10 group.

## 3. Conclusion

This ranking may be of interest to investors who prioritize **historical risk-adjusted efficiency** in low-cost, transparent UCITS ETF structures — particularly those already comfortable with concentrated sector or single-country (US) equity exposure, and for whom low TER and Irish UCITS domicile/tax treatment are relevant selection factors.

**It is important to state explicitly that this is a historical, backward-looking 3-year risk/return ranking based on daily price data with a 0% risk-free rate assumption. It does not constitute a buy recommendation, is not indicative of future performance, and past Sharpe ratios or returns should not be interpreted as a projection of how any of these funds will perform going forward.** Sector concentration, currency exposure and market-cycle dependency observed in this set are factors that merit independent consideration outside the scope of this historical ranking.
